wu: New Year Timeline: Students draw a line on the board from December 31 to January 1. They add 3 personal events (e.g., 'I was at a party', 'I was tired') and 3 class events (e.g., 'We were in class').
wuAlt: Resolution Relay: Teams race to write 5 New Year resolutions on the board using 'will' and 'going to'.
Memory Chain: One student says 'Yesterday I was...', next student repeats and adds their own, chain continues.
pres: Show a dramatic New Year's Eve story comic strip on the board. Highlight 'was/were' and past continuous (e.g., 'The fireworks were exploding'). Elicit and model 5 sentences. Check with thumbs-up/down if sentences are true.
presAlt: Use two photos: one of last year, one of this year. Ask 'Who was there? What were they doing?' to contrast.
Play a short audio of a chaotic New Year's story. Students draw what they hear, focusing on 'was/were' actions.
prac: Past Tense Bingo: Cards have sentences like 'She was dancing'. Teacher calls out prompts ('At midnight...'). Students mark and say the full sentence. Support with sentence frames on the board.
pracAlt: Find Someone Who...: Students walk around asking 'Were you at a party?' and writing names. Winners share 3 findings.
Grammar Auction: Teams bid on correct/incorrect 'was/were' sentences. They must explain errors.
ls: Listen to a 1-minute dramatic story about a disastrous New Year's Eve. Students complete a gap-fill with 'was/were' and past continuous verbs. Check answers in pairs.
re: Freeze Drama: Teacher calls out a New Year scene (e.g., 'Countdown!'). Students freeze in a pose and say what they were doing ('I was screaming').
prod: Write-Swap: Students write a dramatic 2-paragraph opening about a past New Year (e.g., 'Last year, I was at home...'). Swap with a partner, add one past continuous sentence, and return. Groups vote for the most dramatic story.
rw: Read a short PET-style story extract about a childhood New Year. Underline all 'was/were' and past continuous verbs. In pairs, discuss why the author chose those tenses for drama.
st: Read a funny New Year's folktale from Morocco. Close with the goodbye routine: 'Today we told dramatic past stories—great job! Thank you, class.'
g: Teams race to put 6 event cards in order, saying sentences like 'First, we were eating.'
Students write 3 resolutions, vote for class top 5, and present with 'I will...' or 'I am going to...'
Students act out 'was/were' actions (e.g., 'was sleeping') for others to guess.
Teams bid on correct/incorrect sentences, explaining errors.
Students ask 'Were you...?' and write 3 true findings.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a third paragraph for their story with a surprise ending.
Support: Use a word bank with 'was/were' and past continuous verbs for the writing task.
hw: Record a 90-second video saying 3 childhood memories using 'was/were'.
Write 5 resolutions: 3 with 'will', 2 with 'going to', and explain why.
Interview a family member about their New Year's Eve and write 3 sentences.
tip: Use local context: Reference Moroccan New Year (Amazigh new year) to contrast with Western celebrations, making grammar more relatable.
